title: eval_run
description: The machine-readable score of one run against one gold set. `caveats` is deliberately part of the data, not just the rendered page: a caveat you have to remember is a caveat that gets dropped. Rates are objects, never bare floats, so an undefined value (n = 0) can never be mistaken for zero, and every rate names the population its denominator was drawn from so two rates with the same n cannot be confused. `eligibility` records the cases that were NOT scored and why; they stay in the record, because deleting them would quietly make the set easier.

n_unresolved.description: Cases with null gold verdict, excluded from every denominator.

n_excluded_drift.description: Cases excluded because a cited source's availability changed since the set was frozen.

eligibility.description: Which cases were scored and why the rest were not. Excluded cases remain in `per_case` and are rendered in their own report section.

detail.description: Computed from the data, never a constant sentence.

refs_verification.description: Sources whose availability could not be checked. Reported, NOT excluded: unverifiable is not the same as wrong.

populations.description: Every denominator in the record, computed independently of the metrics. Each rate names one of these; a denominator that has drifted from the population it claims fails a test instead of printing a plausible number.

unmatched_gold.description: Derived reasons: extraction_gap (the tool's own audit flagged the label), ambiguous (a contest the aligner refused to decide), attribution_undetermined (the tool's coverage audit could not be read, so blame cannot be assigned to either side), otherwise alignment_failure_or_paraphrase_drift.

macro_f1.description: F1 is undefined only when a class appears in NEITHER column of J (nothing predicted it and no gold instance reached J). A class that is present and always wrong scores 0.0 and stays in the mean; excluding it would delete the run's failures from its own grade.

exclusions.description: Replaces the former `excluded_reason`, which was one constant sentence covering every exclusion and was therefore false whenever the class was present but eliminated.

kind.description: Derived from the counts in `counts`, never asserted.

rate.description: A fraction that remembers its denominator and where the denominator came from. `value` is null when n = 0 — undefined, not zero. `population` keys into the record's `populations` block: two rates with n = 4, one over M and one over J_gold, are otherwise indistinguishable in JSON.
